questions.q: Which pandas expression gives the number of missing values in each column of df?
options: df.isna().sum()
df.dropna().count()
df.fillna(0).sum()
df.isna().unique()
questions.explain: isna() marks each missing cell True; sum() adds those Trues per column. Chain mean() instead to get the share of missing values.

questions.q: The T-SQL condition WHERE age IS NULL corresponds to which pandas filter?
options: df[df["age"] == None]
df[df["age"].isna()]
df[df["age"] == 0]
df.dropna(subset=["age"])
questions.explain: Filtering with a boolean mask from isna() keeps the rows where age is missing. dropna(subset=["age"]) does the opposite: it removes them.

questions.q: In the lesson's 8-row customer table, calling df.dropna() with no arguments leaves 3 rows, while dropna(subset=["monthly_spend"]) leaves 6. What is the takeaway?
options: Dropping any row with any gap can remove far more data than you intended; use subset to target the columns that matter
dropna() always keeps exactly 3 rows
subset makes dropna() fill the gaps instead of deleting rows
Dropping rows is always better than filling them
questions.explain: By default dropna() removes a row if any column is missing. Naming the relevant columns with subset limits the loss.

questions.q: Why did the lesson add an age_missing flag column before filling age with the median?
options: fillna() will not run unless a flag column exists
The median can only be computed on a boolean column
So you can still tell which ages were real and which were filled in
Flag columns make the DataFrame faster
questions.explain: After a fill, filled values look identical to real ones. A flag preserves that information for later analysis.

questions.q: A blank cancel_date column in a subscriptions table most likely means the customer is still active. How should you treat these missing values?
options: Drop all those rows because they are incomplete
Fill them with the median date
Fill them with the earliest date in the column
Keep them, because the gap carries meaning (still active); consider creating an is_active column instead of filling
questions.explain: When missingness is informative, filling or dropping destroys the signal. Capture it explicitly instead.
